blocks.html: An 11-day Tanzania safari at a relaxed, comfortable pace [Favourite for 50+]

blocks.orig: From logistics to lodges, from activities to adventures: everything is taken care of when you head into the Tanzania holiday you’ve dreamed of your whole life.
blocks.html: Lodges, logistics, activities and adventures: we arrange all of it, so you can simply set off on the Tanzania holiday you have been dreaming of for years.

blocks.orig: You kick things off in Arusha with a relaxing day at the pool or exploring the vibrant city. Then the time has come to go out and explore: in your private and comfortable 4×4, you first enjoy the beauties of Tarangire National Park – the kingdom of elephants – during an exhilarating game drive. Want to take a break and walk around for a few minutes? No problem! This is your safari, and you determine the pace.
blocks.html: Your trip begins in Arusha, where you can spend a laid-back day by the pool or wander through the lively city. After that it is time to head out: from your own comfortable private 4×4 you take in Tarangire National Park, the realm of the elephants, on a thrilling game drive. Fancy stretching your legs for a few minutes? That is fine. It is your safari, so you set the pace.

blocks.orig: At Gibb’s Farm, you can find out how coffee is planted, harvested, and roasted. Of course, you’ll also enjoy a cup yourself, as well as a lunch with local delicacies. With this new energy, you dive into the famous Ngorongoro Conservation Area, which welcomes you not only with stunning landscapes but also with the highest wildlife density on the continent. One highlight chases the next when you head to the Serengeti. Keep your eyes open for the Big Five and witness millions of wildebeest and zebras galloping through the endless plains during the Great Wildebeest Migration.
blocks.html: Gibb’s Farm shows you how coffee is grown, picked and roasted, and naturally you get to drink a cup too, along with a lunch of local specialities. Refreshed, you continue to the well-known Ngorongoro Conservation Area, where breathtaking scenery meets the greatest density of wildlife in Africa. The highlights keep coming as you travel on to the Serengeti. Look out for the Big Five and watch, during the Great Wildebeest Migration, as millions of wildebeest and zebras thunder across the seemingly endless plains.

blocks.orig: In between these unforgettable experiences, you relax at comfortable lodges that spoil you with peace, quiet, and all kinds of amenities. At a jewellery making workshop at Shanga, you can let your creativity run wild and create some souvenirs for your loved ones (or yourself). But to be honest, it will be the memories that you will cherish forever.
blocks.html: Between these memorable moments you unwind at comfortable lodges offering calm, quiet and plenty of facilities. During a jewellery making workshop at Shanga you can give your creativity free rein and make a few souvenirs for the people at home (or for yourself). Honestly, though, it is the memories you will treasure most.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear from many travellers is when to go to Tanzania. The truth is that no single answer fits everyone: it comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to travel, your budget and your interests. You will find a detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our safaris you get the chance to discover Tanzania’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each day’s safari begins and finishes, and our experienced guides are happy to help you decide on the day itself. Perhaps you want to see the animals when they are most active around sunrise and sunset, while the temperatures are mild, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool: the choice is yours. Because Tanzania’s varied wildlife is active at different times of day, you’ll have many chances to watch animals on the move.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is well known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. You can watch these impressive animals (lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo) in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, travellers will find Tanzania a safe and friendly destination. The atmosphere is welcoming, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with peace of mind. People are friendly, and it is always sensible to take ordinary precautions such as watching your belongings, just as you would anywhere else in the world. Thanks to Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people, it is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: As you walk out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide greets you with a big smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' The guide takes you straight to your hotel, where you can relax and take in the African atmosphere. The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. Enjoy the luxury of your own safari jeep and take the liberty to stop and watch the animals as long as you like!
blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your own Your Tanzania Trip guide is there with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. On the following day your guide sets off with you on an exclusive private safari, so you can travel at whatever pace suits you. You have the luxury of your own safari jeep and are free to stop and watch the animals for as long as you wish!

blocks.orig: Today is a wonderful relaxing day, that you can spend in whatever way you like. Choose to spend the whole day at the lodge to enjoy the excellent service, sip on refreshing drinks, lounge near the pool, and just engulf yourself in the African vibes surrounding you. Or get to know Arusha through some interesting activities - go for example on a city tour, explore the outskirts of the city by mountain bike, or score your first souvenirs at an exhilarating Maasai market…
blocks.html: Today is a lovely day of rest, and how you fill it is up to you. You could stay at the lodge all day, enjoying the excellent service, sipping cool drinks, lazing by the pool and taking in the African atmosphere around you. Alternatively, discover Arusha through a few interesting activities - take a city tour, for instance, cycle through the outskirts on a mountain bike, or pick up your first souvenirs at a lively Maasai market…

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its large herds of elephants and its great number of giant baobab trees. These trees can reach an age of several hundred years, and in the dry season elephants actually use them as a water source, drawing water out of them with a special technique. On top of that, the Tarangire River is the only water source during the dry season, which is why you can see herds of up to 250 elephants here at that time of year, alongside many other animals!

blocks.orig: Gibb's Farm offers the old-age rhythm of an African farm and coffee plantation, right on the slopes of Ngorongoro Highlands. Walk around on this sanctuary of peace and tranquility, and watch vegetables being harvested, coffee roasted, cows milked, and pigs fed. The vegetable gardens, fruit trees, and herbs provide inspiration for the farm's chefs, who in their turn amaze visitors with a delicious lunch. A little piece of heaven!
blocks.html: On the slopes of the Ngorongoro Highlands, Gibb's Farm keeps the age-old rhythm of an African farm and coffee plantation alive. Stroll around this peaceful, tranquil sanctuary and see vegetables being picked, coffee being roasted, cows being milked and pigs being fed. The farm's chefs draw inspiration from the vegetable gardens, fruit trees and herbs, and in turn they delight visitors with a delicious lunch. A small slice of paradise!

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The renowned Ngorongoro Crater ranks among Africa's seven natural wonders. It came into being two million years ago, when a huge volcano erupted. The rich volcanic soil gave rise to a unique ecosystem that now supports the highest density of animals anywhere in Africa! Down in the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the scenery is so spectacular that you won’t know where to look first!

blocks.orig: You fly into the Serengeti, where your guide will be waiting for you. This marks the start of your safari in an ecosystem famous for its endless plains, the Great Migration, and one of Africa's highest concentrations of lions and cheetahs.
blocks.html: A flight takes you into the Serengeti, where your guide is ready and waiting. Here your safari begins, in an ecosystem known for its vast plains, the Great Migration and one of the greatest concentrations of lions and cheetahs in Africa.

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park has a reputation as the place for a safari, largely thanks to the Great Migration that moves through the park. The huge, charging herds are a remarkable sight, and so is the large population of predators: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! Add to that many other beautiful animals, which your guide will gladly look for with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: You will take a scenic flight to Arusha, a vibrant city that serves as the gateway to Tanzania's northern safari circuit - located at the base of the towering Mount Meru.
blocks.html: A scenic flight brings you to Arusha, the lively gateway city to Tanzania's northern safari circuit, which lies at the foot of the towering Mount Meru.

blocks.orig: Dive into the world of beads and jewellery in an exclusive two-and-a-half-hour workshop at Shanga, a social enterprise in Arusha. The company employs over thirty, mostly hearing-impaired artisans who create high-quality handmade jewellery, glassware, and homeware with recycled and sustainable materials. Embark on the workshop with a guided tour through the premises, then test your creativity by crafting two pieces of jewellery and trying your hand at glass blowing.
blocks.html: Immerse yourself in beads and jewellery during an exclusive workshop of two and a half hours at Shanga, a social enterprise in Arusha. More than thirty artisans, most of them hearing-impaired, work here making high-quality handmade jewellery, glassware, and homeware from recycled and sustainable materials. The workshop starts with a guided tour of the site, after which you put your creativity to the test by making two pieces of jewellery and having a go at glass blowing.

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax in the lodge a bit longer before heading to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can enjoy the lodge a little longer before transferring to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for your journey home. Not quite ready to leave? You can also extend your holiday by a few days on one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
